resources.string: Collects this app\'s own log, versions, settings and the devices found into one file and opens the share sheet. Nothing is sent automatically; you choose where it goes.
Why can\'t I find my TV?
Checks Wi-Fi, router and TV searches and explains what is wrong
CastApp is installed from GitHub, so it checks there. Only github.com is contacted and nothing about you is sent.
Looks once a day when the app starts
CastApp is allowed to run in the background. Tap for phone-specific tips.
Needed so casting a file keeps playing with the screen off
Turns on Do Not Disturb while the screen is mirrored and puts your previous mode back afterwards. Android 15 and newer already hide sensitive notifications in screen shares.
Allow CastApp under \"Do Not Disturb access\" in the next screen, then come back.
Why can\'t I find my TV?
Checking your network… this takes about 6 seconds.
The phone is not connected to any network. Connect it to the same Wi-Fi as your TV.
Casting only works over Wi-Fi: phone and TV must be on the same network. Switch Wi-Fi on and connect to your home network.
The phone has no address on a local network. Reconnect to Wi-Fi, or switch Wi-Fi off and on. If a VPN is running, turn it off.
A VPN often hides the local network, so TVs are not found. Pause the VPN (or allow local network access in the VPN app) while casting.
The phone (%1$s) could not reach the router. The Wi-Fi may have no real connection, or it is a guest network. Reconnect, or move closer to the router.

No TV or other device replied to the searches. Guest networks and \"AP isolation\" (also called client isolation) block casting; so can a router that filters multicast. Check that the TV is switched on and on the same Wi-Fi, switch off AP isolation in the router, or try \"Add by IP\" with the TV\'s address.
Chromecast and AirPlay search got no answer

Google Cast and AirPlay devices are found with mDNS, and nothing replied. Smart TVs found another way still work. If a Chromecast or Apple TV is missing, the router may block multicast: look for \"IGMP snooping\" or \"multicast\" settings, or use \"Add by IP\".
The DLNA search got no answer
No smart TV (DLNA) replied to the search. If your TV is a Samsung, LG, Sony or Philips model, check that it is on, awake and on this Wi-Fi.
These TVs did not answer: %1$s. They may be off, asleep or on another network. Switch them on (a TV in standby can be woken with \"Wake up\" in its menu), then search again.

%1$s has an address outside this Wi-Fi\'s network. Phone and TV need to be on the same network; for example, the TV may be on Ethernet behind another router, or the phone on a guest or 5 GHz network with a separate address range.
TV reachable but does not answer searches
%1$s can be reached directly but did not answer the search. Multicast is probably blocked on this network. Use \"Scan network\" or \"Add by IP\"; remembered TVs stay in the list.
Android\'s Data Saver can limit background network use. If casting stops by itself, turn it off or allow CastApp unrestricted data.
Battery Saver slows down or stops background work, which can interrupt casting with the screen off. Turn it off while casting.
The network is set up correctly for casting. If something still fails, use \"Send debug log\" in Settings.
Keep playing with the screen off
When you cast a video or music file, CastApp plays it from this phone. To keep that going with the screen off, Android must not put the app to sleep. Allow it to run without battery restrictions.
CastApp is already allowed to run in the background.
Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO: open Settings > Apps > Manage apps > CastApp, switch on \"Autostart\", then open \"Battery saver\" and choose \"No restrictions\".
Samsung: open Settings > Battery > Background usage limits, and make sure CastApp is not in \"Sleeping apps\" or \"Deep sleeping apps\". Add it to \"Never sleeping apps\".
Huawei / Honor: open Settings > Apps > App launch > CastApp, switch to \"Manage manually\" and allow Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.
OnePlus / Oppo / Realme: open Settings > Battery > CastApp (or App battery management) and allow background activity; also switch on \"Allow auto-launch\" if you see it.
GitHub says there is no published release. Either no release exists yet, or the repository is private. You can open the releases page to look yourself.
This release has no CastApp.apk file. Open the releases page to download it.
Android needs your permission before CastApp can install the update. Allow \"Install unknown apps\" for CastApp on the next screen, come back and tap Download again.
Sends a Wake-on-LAN signal to %1$s, then searches again
Set MAC address to wake up
Needed to wake the TV from standby. Find it in the TV\'s network settings; the TV must have Wake-on-LAN switched on.
Not a valid MAC address. Example: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
